notes:
CRM notes (shorthand):
- Company: MosaicOnboard — mid-market UX platform building guided product onboarding copilot inside web/mobile app.
- Primary buyer: CTO (Elena Park) + Head of Product (Jamal Rivers).
- Use-case: short guided flows (4-8 turns), heavy function-calls to customer profile + account state, some async agent workflows for complex flows.
- POC summary: ran 2-week hosted API POC. Good integration speed. Streaming + first-token latency fine (median ~180ms). Problem: p95 spikes ~800-950ms during traffic bursts -> degrades perceived responsiveness for in-app microflows.
- Cost target: token-cost cap per session, want predictable per-session pricing. Internal target ~= $0.015-$0.03 per active user session. Asking for suggestions: prefix caching for repeated prompts, smaller quantized model variants for fallback.
- Interested in path: start hosted API (fast dev), then move to Dedicated reserved pool to get consistent p95 and capacity predictability. Also wants routing fallback (cheaper quantized variant) for non-critical flows.
- Security: SSO/SAML required, SOC2 mandatory, KMS for customer-managed keys for EU customers; data residency for EU/UK users (legal wants contractual language).
- Quote ask: dedicated capacity pricing + canary deployment plan (1 AZ canary, then 3-AZ scale). Also want SLA language for p95 latency targets and escalation path.
- Quote/Docs linked: dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf; SecFAQ-MosaicOnboard.pdf.
- AE notes: "We can get p95 improvements with dedicated pools + autoscale rules + prefix caching; need to confirm quantized fallback latency tradeoffs."
- SE notes: "Batching helped cost but increased tail in some patterns; prefer continuous batching knobs + per-route SLOs."
- Customer quote: "Latency consistency is make-or-break for our onboarding UX — spikes lead to drop-off."
- Next: deliver dedicated proposal, schedule 60-min security deep-dive with infra/security (deliver SOC2 + KMS flow).
- Blockers: procurement timeline (procurement meets 11/28), legal review on data residency, final SOC2 artifact.
